text:
Non emergono contraddizioni interne dirette tra le righe 1-10, poiché ogni pratica riporta un budget univoco e uno stato coerente con la propria descrizione. Tuttavia, la Riga 11 introduce una distinzione fondamentale: gli importi sono **preventivi**, non consuntivi.

Differenze chiave:
1. **Natura dei dati**: I budget (es. 6647€ per P10-000) sono stime preliminari, non costi finali confermati.
2. **Coerenza temporale**: Le scadenze sono definite per tutte le pratiche tranne P10-006 ("da definire"), creando un'asimmetria operativa.
3. **Stato vs. Azione**: Pratiche "approvate" (es. P10-000) e "sospese" (es. P10-001) condividono la stessa dipendenza dal disegno aggiornato, il che può generare conflitti di priorità se le risorse sono limitate, ma non costituisce una contraddizione logica nei dati forniti.<|im_end|>
prompt_en:
Look for internal contradictions and differences between proposed and confirmed budgets.

Document (fictional data):
Line 1. Nadia, responsible for the building services department, reports case P10-000, status approved, budget 6647 euros, deadline 2026-11-11. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 2. Paolo, responsible for the structures department, reports case P10-001, status suspended, budget 3802 euros, deadline 2026-11-12. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 3. Rita, responsible for the construction department, reports case P10-002, status under review, budget 6654 euros, deadline 2026-11-13. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 4. Sara, responsible for the building services department, reports case P10-003, status approved, budget 2249 euros, deadline 2026-11-14. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 5. Tommaso, responsible for the structures department, reports case P10-004, status approved, budget 3622 euros, deadline 2026-11-15. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 6. Anna, responsible for the construction department, reports case P10-005, status suspended, budget 4669 euros, deadline 2026-11-16. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 7. Bruno, responsible for the building services department, reports case P10-006, status under review, budget 8823 euros, deadline to be defined. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 8. Carla, responsible for the structures department, reports case P10-007, status approved, budget 6572 euros, deadline 2026-11-18. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 9. Diego, responsible for the construction department, reports case P10-008, status approved, budget 2948 euros, deadline 2026-11-19. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 10. Elena, responsible for the building services department, reports case P10-009, status suspended, budget 2267 euros, deadline 2026-11-20. The review depends on the availability of the updated drawing.
Line 11. The proposal to bring all deadlines forward has not been approved. The stated amounts are estimates, not actual costs.

Keep the answer concise: at most about 120 words, or the requested code or data. Do not include internal reasoning.

answer_en:
No direct internal contradictions emerge between the 1-10 lines, since each file reports a unique budget and a status consistent with its description. However, Line 11 introduces a fundamental distinction: the amounts are **estimated**, not final.

Key Differences:
1. **Nature of data**: Budgets (e.g. 6647€ for P10-000) are preliminary estimates, not confirmed final costs.
2. **Time consistency**: Deadlines are defined for all cases except P10-006 ("to be defined"), creating an operational asymmetry.
3. **State vs. Action**: "Approved" (e.g. P10-000) and "suspended" (e.g. P10-001) practices share the same dependency on the updated design, which may generate priority conflicts if resources are limited, but does not constitute a logical contradiction in the data provided.<|im_end|>
